_comment: Candidate local models for start_litellm_proxy.sh's interactive menu, served via mlx_vlm.server (not Ollama — see LITELLM_PROXY_USAGE.md for why). Every entry here has been through verify_max_kv_size.sh with verdict SAFE before being added; do not add a model to this file without running that script first. 'display' fields are shown to the user when picking a model, in plain language they can act on without reading the underlying research docs.

_schema_notes.size_gb: Real on-disk size, measured directly (du -sh on the cached HF repo), not estimated from quantization bit-width.
_schema_notes.max_context_architectural: The model's trained/architectural context ceiling, read from its own config.json (max_position_embeddings). This is NOT the same as a safe operating context on any given machine — see recommended_max_kv_size_gb_tier (pending) once real-load memory testing is done.
_schema_notes.verification: Result of verify_max_kv_size.sh — confirms mlx_vlm.server's --max-kv-size admission gate actually rejects oversized requests for this model rather than silently ignoring them (the failure mode Ollama's MLX runner has, unfixably, per LITELLM_ROUTING_PLAN.md §4.15 and upstream Ollama issue discussion). It does NOT confirm real long-context memory safety — that needs a separate near-cap-fill test (LITELLM_ROUTING_PLAN.md §4.14 methodology) not yet run for any model in this file.
_schema_notes.tool_calling: Whether OpenCode/Claude Code's tool calls (webfetch, bash, edit, etc.) actually come back as a structured, parseable tool_calls response instead of silently degrading to plain chat text. Determined by LIVE testing (real /v1/chat/completions request with a tool schema attached, temperature=0), not by static inspection of the chat template or by which mlx_vlm tool_parser gets auto-assigned — several models (the whole qwen2.5-coder-*-instruct family) get assigned a parser (json_tools) that matches their template's markers, yet still fail live because the model itself doesn't reliably emit the <tool_call> tags its own template instructs it to use. That specific failure was independently reproduced on TWO OTHER serving stacks besides mlx_vlm (vLLM — see github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-Coder/issues/180 — and Ollama/llama.cpp, tested directly on this machine 2026-09-28), confirming it's a property of the model's own fine-tuning, not a bug in any one harness. phi-4-mini-instruct-4bit is the opposite case: Microsoft's own model card documents real function-calling support and benchmarks it on Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard, but mlx_vlm's tool_parsers registry (mlx_vlm/tool_parsers/__init__.py's _TEMPLATE_MARKERS) has no entry matching Phi's <|tool|>/<|tool_call|> token format, so mlx_vlm never even tries to parse its output — a serving-stack gap, not a model capability gap (vLLM has a dedicated --tool-call-parser phi4_mini_json for this exact model, merged via vllm-project/vllm#14886). KNOWN GAP: model_advisor.py does NOT yet read this field — the interactive picker will still recommend qwen2.5-coder-*-instruct or phi-4-mini-instruct-4bit for coding tasks without warning that tool use (webfetch, bash, edit, etc. from OpenCode/Claude Code) will silently no-op on them. Same pattern as max_context_verified_safe's documented gap above; fixing both in model_advisor.py at the same time would make sense.

display.good_for: Verifying the local model stack works end to end, and instant replies to trivial one-off questions. Not a real coding assistant — too small to trust with anything you'd actually ship.
usage_examples: "Reply with exactly the word: pong" — smoke-test that opencode/Claude Code → LiteLLM → MLX is wired up correctly before loading a bigger model
"What's the syntax for a Python list comprehension?" — quick trivia lookup, not real code generation
display.known_issues: Too small for real coding work — expect frequent mistakes on anything beyond a trivial snippet. Use only to test the pipeline itself, never as a daily driver.

verification.notes: Admission gate verified at 32/256/1024-token bounds. Real long-context memory load not stress-tested, but model is small enough this is low risk.

tool_calling.method: Live /v1/chat/completions request against a real mlx_vlm.server instance with a web_search tool schema attached, temperature=0.
tool_calling.notes: Correctly returned finish_reason=tool_calls with a well-formed function call (name + JSON arguments) on the first attempt, despite being the smallest model in this list (0.6GB) — structural tool-call support is not a function of model size for this family.

display.good_for: Simple coding help on a memory-constrained machine — function-level edits, boilerplate, and short scripts. The conservative fallback on a 16GB Mac if the 7B model feels too tight alongside other running apps.
usage_examples: "Write a Python function that parses this CSV format and returns a list of dicts" — clear-spec utility code
"Explain what this 20-line function does" — code comprehension on a short, self-contained snippet
display.known_issues: 32K architectural context ceiling — will not hold a large repo's AGENTS.md plus several file reads without hitting the limit. Struggles with complex multi-file reasoning; keep tasks scoped to one file/function at a time. ❌ TOOL CALLS DO NOT WORK: confirmed broken on THREE separate serving stacks (mlx_vlm, vLLM, and Ollama/llama.cpp) — the model ignores its own chat template's <tool_call> instructions and instead wraps attempted calls in <tools>/<response> tags that no parser recognizes, so OpenCode/Claude Code tool use (webfetch, bash, edit, etc.) silently falls back to plain chat text. Do not use for agentic/tool-using work — see tool_calling below.

verification.notes: Admission gate verified at 32/256/1024-token bounds. Real long-context memory load not yet stress-tested.

tool_calling.method: Live /v1/chat/completions request against a real mlx_vlm.server instance with a web_search tool schema attached, temperature=0 (repeated 3x, deterministic). Independently re-confirmed via Ollama 0.33.2 (qwen2.5-coder:3b-instruct, Q4_K_M GGUF) through both its OpenAI-compat and native /api/chat endpoints.
tool_calling.tool_parser: json_tools (auto-assigned by mlx_vlm — template matches, model output doesn't)
tool_calling.notes: finish_reason=stop every time, tool_calls always null/absent. Model echoes the tool schema back wrapped in <tools></tools> then attempts the call wrapped in <response>{...}</response> — never uses the <tool_call></tool_call> tags its own chat template explicitly instructs it to use. Same failure independently reported by a third party against vLLM: github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-Coder/issues/180. This is a property of the model's fine-tuning, confirmed across 3 independent serving stacks — not fixable by switching harnesses.

display.tagline: Small general-purpose model with a large context window
display.good_for: General assistant tasks and long-document Q&A on a tight-memory machine — its 128K architectural ceiling is unusually large for a 2GB model. Not coder-specialized, so treat it as an alternative to the Qwen-Coder models rather than a replacement.
usage_examples: "Summarize the key changes in this 5,000-line log file" — long-document analysis that would overflow the 32K-context coder models
"Rewrite this paragraph to be more concise" — general writing/instruction-following, not code-specific
display.known_issues: Not coding-specialized — likely to underperform the Qwen2.5-Coder models on actual code generation despite the larger context window. Use for long-context or general tasks, not as your primary coding model. ❌ TOOL CALLS DO NOT WORK ON THIS STACK: Microsoft's model card documents real function-calling support for this model (benchmarked on Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard), but mlx_vlm has no parser for Phi's <|tool|>/<|tool_call|> token format, so it never even attempts to parse tool calls out of this model's output — see tool_calling below. Do not use for agentic/tool-using work on this setup.

verification.notes: Admission gate verified at 32/256/1024-token bounds. Real long-context memory load not yet stress-tested — worth particular attention given its 128K architectural ceiling is 4x the Qwen-Coder models'.

tool_calling.method: Live /v1/chat/completions request against a real mlx_vlm.server instance with a web_search tool schema attached.
tool_calling.tool_parser: none — mlx_vlm's _infer_tool_parser() returned None for this model's chat template
tool_calling.notes: finish_reason=stop, tool_calls=null, prompt_tokens was suspiciously small (26) meaning the tool schema wasn't even rendered into the prompt — model just answered from its own knowledge ('I can't perform web searches...'). This is a SERVING-STACK GAP, not a model limitation: Phi-4-mini's own added_tokens.json has dedicated <|tool|>/<|/tool|>/<|tool_call|>/<|/tool_call|>/<|tool_response|> tokens and Microsoft explicitly documents + benchmarks function-calling support for this exact model. vLLM has a dedicated --tool-call-parser phi4_mini_json for it (merged vllm-project/vllm#14886), but that parser has no mlx_vlm equivalent, and vLLM itself has no real Apple Silicon GPU acceleration (multiple Metal/MPS PRs abandoned as of 2026-09), so switching stacks just to fix this specific model isn't practical on this machine.

display.tagline: More capable coder, extra-quantized to save memory
display.good_for: A step up in coding capability from the 3B model, at nearly the same memory footprint as the 4-bit 7B thanks to 3-bit quantization. Consider this over the 4-bit version specifically when memory is the binding constraint.
usage_examples: "Refactor this function to handle the edge case where the input list is empty" — multi-step reasoning within a single file
"Write unit tests for this function covering the main cases" — test generation for existing code
display.known_issues: 3-bit quantization trades some accuracy for size — expect occasional subtle mistakes the 4-bit sibling wouldn't make (wrong variable name, off-by-one, slightly wrong logic branch). Same 32K architectural ceiling as the 4-bit version. Prefer the 4-bit variant when the extra ~0.9GB isn't the deciding factor. ❌ TOOL CALLS DO NOT WORK: same Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct family failure as the 3B/4bit/14B siblings — see tool_calling below and qwen2.5-coder-3b-instruct-4bit's notes for the cross-stack confirmation.

verification.notes: Admission gate verified at 32/256/1024-token bounds, after fixing a real script bug (a stale server process from a prior failed download briefly caused a false reading — see verify_max_kv_size.sh's wait_for_port_free/served-model check, added specifically because of this incident). Real long-context memory load not yet stress-tested.

tool_calling.notes: finish_reason=stop, tool_calls=null. Model wrapped its attempted call in a ```json code block instead of the <tool_call></tool_call> tags its own template instructs — a different wrong format than the 3B (<tools>/<response>) and 4bit (```xml/<tools>) siblings, but the same underlying failure: this whole model family doesn't reliably follow its own tool-call output format regardless of quantization.

display.good_for: Real coding capability without the memory pressure of the 9B+ models — the primary recommendation for a 16GB MacBook Pro. Enough headroom left over for KV cache, the OS, and normal background apps.
usage_examples: "Implement a REST endpoint that validates this payload and writes it to the database" — moderately complex, multi-step feature work
"Review this diff and point out any bugs or style issues" — code review on a realistic-sized change
display.known_issues: 32K architectural ceiling means a large repo's AGENTS.md plus a long conversation history will need compaction sooner than a 128K-class model would. Not yet stress-tested at real long-context memory load (only the admission gate is verified). ❌ TOOL CALLS DO NOT WORK: same Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct family failure as the 3B/3bit/14B siblings — see tool_calling below.

verification.notes: Admission gate verified at 32/256/1024-token bounds, after fixing a real script bug (see qwen2.5-coder-7b-instruct-3bit's note — same incident, same fix applies to this model's result too since both were retested after the fix). Real long-context memory load not yet stress-tested.

tool_calling.method: Live /v1/chat/completions request against a real mlx_vlm.server instance with a web_search tool schema attached, temperature=0.
tool_calling.tool_parser: json_tools (auto-assigned by mlx_vlm — template matches, model output doesn't)
tool_calling.notes: finish_reason=stop, tool_calls=null. Model wrapped its attempted call in ```xml fenced <tools></tools> tags instead of the <tool_call></tool_call> tags its own template instructs — yet another wrong format, distinct from the 3bit sibling's plain ```json block. Confirms this is a per-generation-sampling issue with the model's fine-tuning, not a deterministic template bug that a fixed prompt tweak would solve.

display.good_for: The lightest multimodal (vision-capable) option in this list — fills the gap between the tiny text-only models and the 12B+ multimodal models. "E4B" is Gemma's elastic/MatFormer naming (effective ~4B capacity), not a typo for a plain 4B model.
usage_examples: "What does this error dialog screenshot say, and how do I fix it?" — lightweight vision Q&A without the memory cost of the 12B multimodal model
"Summarize this scanned receipt/document image" — small-scale multimodal tasks on a 16-24GB Mac
display.known_issues: 131K architectural ceiling — smaller than the plain 12B/26B Gemma-4 models (262K), since this elastic variant trades some capacity for its smaller footprint. As an elastic/MatFormer model, its internal cache-building path differs from the plain Gemma-4 models — verified separately rather than assumed safe by analogy.

verification.notes: Admission gate verified at 32/256/1024-token bounds. First elastic/MatFormer-architecture model tested — passed despite having a different cache-building path than the plain gemma-4-12b/26b models, which was worth checking rather than assuming.

models.architecture: qwen3 (plain, not qwen3_5's hybrid linear/full-attention design)

display.good_for: A capable general-purpose model distinct from both the Qwen2.5-Coder family (coding-specialized) and Qwen3.5 (hybrid attention architecture) already in this list — genuine architectural diversity, not just a different size of something we already have.
usage_examples: "Help me think through the tradeoffs of these two approaches" — general reasoning, not code-specific
"Draft a design doc for this feature" — writing/planning tasks alongside coding work
display.known_issues: 40,960-token architectural ceiling — smaller than Qwen3.5's 262K and Phi-4-mini's 131K, but larger than the Qwen2.5-Coder models' 32K. Not coding-specialized, so expect the Qwen2.5-Coder-14B model to outperform it on actual code generation despite similar size.

verification.notes: Admission gate verified at 32/256/1024-token bounds. First plain-qwen3 architecture tested (distinct from qwen2 and qwen3_5, both already covered elsewhere in this list) — no prior model in this list shared this exact architecture, so this result carries no assumption from analogy.

tool_calling.method: Live /v1/chat/completions request against a real mlx_vlm.server instance with a web_search tool schema attached, temperature=0.
tool_calling.notes: Correctly returned finish_reason=tool_calls with a well-formed function call. Important control result: this model uses the SAME json_tools parser as the entire qwen2.5-coder-*-instruct family (all NOT_SUPPORTED), proving the parser itself works fine — the failure in that family is specific to Qwen2.5-Coder's own fine-tuning, not to json_tools.

display.good_for: A real capability step up from the 7B Coder model for a 24GB Mac — same architecture family and same 32K context ceiling, just more capable at the same coding-specialized task.
usage_examples: "Implement this feature across several files and keep the existing code style" — more demanding multi-file coding tasks than the 7B model handles well
"Debug why this test is failing and fix it" — more reliable reasoning through non-trivial bugs
display.known_issues: Same 32K architectural ceiling as the 3B/7B Coder models in this family — a large repo's AGENTS.md plus a long conversation will still need compaction sooner than a 128K+ class model. Encountered a real download-reliability issue during verification (see verification notes) — resolved by the harness, not a property of the model itself. ❌ TOOL CALLS DO NOT WORK: same Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct family failure as the 3B/3bit/4bit siblings — see tool_calling below.

verification.notes: Admission gate verified at 32/256/1024-token bounds, after fixing a real script bug: repeated health-check timeouts during this model's initial download each killed the in-progress transfer with no resume, leaving 5 abandoned .incomplete blob fragments (8GB) without ever completing the real 7.75GB download. Fixed by adding a standalone snapshot_download() pre-download step to verify_max_kv_size.sh, run before the server (and its kill-on-timeout path) ever touches the model — this fix now applies to every model verified after this one.

display.good_for: The strongest general recommendation once you have 24GB+ of RAM — a real 128K-class context window with the fastest measured MLX throughput of any model in this list (1.7-2.5x faster than its own GGUF counterpart at every context size tested, per prior benchmarking).

display.known_issues: 9.7GB of weights alone is too much on a 16GB Mac — leaves too little headroom for KV cache plus the OS and background apps. Not recommended below 24GB.

models._active_weight_note: Derived from a real live decode-speed benchmark on this machine (103.7 tok/s measured, per HARDWARE_SPEED_ESTIMATION.md §7), working backward through the bandwidth formula — NOT computed purely from config.json's num_experts_per_tok/num_experts=8/128 ratio (which alone gives ~1.0GB, undercounting always-active attention/embedding layers). This is the one MoE model in this list with a real measurement behind its active-weight figure; do not copy this number to any other MoE model without its own benchmark.
models._max_context_verified_safe_note: NOT a formula output — the highest actual prompt_tokens that completed successfully in verify_long_context_memory.sh's real stress test (see below). model_advisor.py does NOT yet consult this field and will still recommend up to max_context_architectural based on free memory alone — see PROJECT_STATUS.md's open items for this known gap.

display.tagline: ❌ CONFIRMED long-context memory-safety failure — do not use above ~28K tokens
display.good_for: Only short/moderate-context coding tasks (well under ~28K prompt tokens) until root-caused. Do NOT use for large-repo or long-session work despite its architectural 262,144-token ceiling — real testing found that ceiling is not safely reachable on this server/quantization combination.
usage_examples: "Implement this one function, given this single file" — short, self-contained coding tasks that stay well under ~28K prompt tokens
NOT RECOMMENDED for large-scale/repo-wide tasks — see known_issues
display.known_issues: CONFIRMED via a real long-context memory stress test (verify_long_context_memory.sh, 2026-09-27), not just the prior unresolved flag: with mlx_vlm.server running this model's actual production flags (--max-kv-size 131072 --kv-bits 8 --kv-group-size 64 --quantized-kv-start 0 --kv-quant-scheme uniform), a 28,276-token prompt completed safely (wired memory settled ~21GB), but a 40,000-token-target prompt and a 58,982-token-target prompt BOTH failed the same way: wired memory grew without bound throughout prefill (not proportional to the token count — both failures happened at a similar ~113-117s elapsed mark despite the different target sizes, suggesting the growth tracks ELAPSED PREFILL TIME/chunk count more than KV-cache size), crossed 38GB, and had to be forcibly killed by monitor_memory.sh's safety net before the request ever completed. Root cause not identified (plausibly a per-prefill-chunk buffer that mlx_vlm.server isn't releasing for this model/quantization combination — not confirmed). Ruling out KV quantization as the sole cause: a separate controlled test confirmed this model recalls a fixed secret correctly at ~28K tokens with BOTH quantized and unquantized KV, so the failure is specific to sustained/longer prefill, not to quantization precision. Full data: mlx_long_context_stress_results.json. DO NOT recommend this model for long-context use, and never run it without monitor_memory.sh (--monitor) active as a safety net, until this is root-caused and either fixed or given a hard verified-safe context cap in this file that model_advisor.py actually enforces.
display.max_context_label: 262,144 tokens (architectural max — NOT safely reachable, see known_issues)

verification.notes: Admission gate verified at 32/256/1024-token bounds — this only confirms max-kv-size rejects oversized short requests correctly. Real long-context memory safety has since been tested (see long_context_verification below) and found UNSAFE — the two verdicts measure different things and are not in conflict.

long_context_verification.method: verify_long_context_memory.sh — escalating near-cap-fill prompts against the SAME production flags start_litellm_proxy.sh uses (max-kv-size 131072, kv-bits 8), with monitor_memory.sh watching the real server PID as the safety net.
long_context_verification.notes: Safe up to 28,276 actual prompt tokens (20% escalation step). Failed at both a 40,000-token-target follow-up probe and the 58,982-token-target (45%) escalation step — unbounded wired-memory growth during prefill, monitor-killed before ~38GB on this 48GB machine. See models.json's known_issues and mlx_long_context_stress_results.json for full detail.

tool_calling.tool_parser: qwen3_coder (this model also ships its own dedicated qwen3coder_tool_parser.py alongside its chat_template.jinja — the only model in this list with a model-specific parser file bundled in its own HF repo)
tool_calling.notes: Correctly returned finish_reason=tool_calls with a well-formed function call on the first attempt. Best-supported tool-calling model in this list on paper (purpose-built agentic/coding model with its own parser), but combine with the long_context_verification UNSAFE verdict above — don't push this model past ~28K prompt tokens regardless of how well tool calling itself works.
